title: Auto-resolve merge conflicts in grounding docs, but only for counts-sentence changes
context: Generated docs (CLAUDE.md, etc.) carry a counts sentence that signals whether the doc is ahead of or lagging behind the stored data. A prior PR wanted to drop this to avoid a doc-ahead defect, but losing the signal removes the only tripwire for fnd_6391b4242f. Developers repeatedly merge conflicting changes to these auto-generated files, making manual resolution expensive.
decision: Implement `merge=hunch-grounding` driver that auto-resolves a hard conflict if and only if every conflicting hunk is confined to the counts sentence (both sides parse valid, nothing else differs). Keep `ours` as placeholder. Leave any conflict outside the counts sentence untouched with diff3 markers. Post-merge hook's `hunch grounding --refresh` self-heals the placeholder counts, reading as 'lagging' (safe) never 'ahead' (dangerous).
consequences: Merge conflicts in the five grounding docs are reduced to the counts sentence and auto-resolved, eliminating manual intervention for the common case.
The doc remains 'lagging' after merge (counts are placeholder), triggering the self-healing refresh hook, preserving the invariant that fnd_6391b4242f depends on.
Any conflict outside the counts sentence (prose, structure, metadata) stays a real conflict, surfaced to the human — safety is not sacrificed for automation.
The signal that the doc lags behind the store is preserved, keeping observability that the prior approach would have removed.
alternatives_rejected: Drop the counts sentence entirely — loses the 'doc ahead' signal that fnd_6391b4242f depends on for detection.
Leave all conflicts to manual resolution — expensive and error-prone for a predictable, append-only sentence.
Do a full text merge of grounding docs — would hide real content conflicts in diff3 markers, making them easy to miss.

rejected_tripwires.alternative: Drop the counts sentence entirely (would lose the doc-lagging signal that prevents the doc-ahead defect)
Accept all merge conflicts in these docs as requiring manual resolution
Implement a looser merge driver that might auto-resolve real content conflicts and obscure issues
